chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the Imprecation (Mubahala),

he (peace be upon him) said: 'Intertwine your fingers with his fingers, then you should say: O Allah! If so-and-so has denied a truth and acknowledged a falsehood, then strike him with a reckoning from the sky or with a punishment from Your Presence, and you should curse him seventy times.'

key_terms.الْمُبَاهَلَةِ: Imprecation; a ritual calling upon God to curse the liar
key_terms.تُشَبِّكُ أَصَابِعَكَ: Intertwine your fingers; a specific physical gesture during the ritual
key_terms.تُلَاعِنُهُ: You curse him; the act of invoking divine curse upon the other party
key_terms.حُسْبَانٍ: Reckoning or strike (often referring to a thunderbolt or sudden punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method and supplication for performing Mubahala according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific ritual mechanics of Mubahala, emphasizing the physical act of intertwining fingers as a sign of mutual commitment to the divine verdict. It provides the precise supplication for invoking Allah’s punishment upon the party that denies truth or acknowledges falsehood, reflecting the Shia scholarly understanding of this practice as a means of resolving disputes through divine intervention.
